Sarah — thanks for sending these over and for the heads-up on notarization. High-level plan from our side:

1) Remote notarization: Redwood accepts e-notarizations that meet U.S. remote online notarization standards (and equivalent EU/UK pivots) as long as Helios provides the notarized PDF + notary certificate. If Helios' signer will use a NL notary that provides a recognized e-notarization certificate, we can accept it. If not, we will fall back to a wet signature for that signer.

2) DocuSign routing: proposed order — Helios primary signer(s) first, Helios witness/COO second (if applicable), Redwood exec last (Redwood CEO/GC). Final clean PDF to be published to both parties plus Redwood legal@redwoodai.com and archived in our contract bucket.

3) Proof of authority: yes, please provide a signer authority attestation (one-page POA or signed board resolution). If Helios prefers, we can accept an emailed attestation from your contracts team and then collect an officer-signed POA at closing.

4) Timeline & escalation: if signatures are not completed within 5 business days of envelope send, we'll escalate to VP Legal to approve a one-time extension.

I'll loop in Legal (Laura) and Ops (Ben) to confirm DocuSign recipient order and to prepare the envelope. Ben — can you own the envelope (create/send) and set conditional routing for a wet-sign fallback? Laura — any legal flags on accepting NL e-notary and the POA language?

Sarah — if that aligns, I will ask Ben to send the envelope and include a DocuSign recipient order in his note.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodai.com
